summary: The reader has an undergraduate computer science education: discrete mathematics (modular arithmetic, primes and coprimality, the Chinese remainder theorem, permutations, induction, recurrences), calculus-level analysis (logarithms, floor and ceiling, norms and rounding errors), linear algebra (vectors, matrices, invertibility, rank, over the reals, complex numbers and F2), and algorithms (asymptotic notation, schoolbook multiplication, divide and conquer, sorting) with a first look at the FFT. They know basic multitape Turing machines and tapes, polynomials and complex numbers including roots of unity. They have not met Schoenhage-Strassen or Karatsuba-level multiplication algorithms in depth, ring and group-algebra language beyond polynomials, tensor products, numerical error analysis of fixed-point transforms, or any research literature on integer multiplication.

known.name: Logarithms and iterated logarithm notation
known.gloss: The base-2 logarithm lg n = ceil(log2 n), its rules (log of a product, change of base), and the meaning of powers such as (lg n)^(1-kappa).

known.name: Big-Omega, Theta and little-o notation
known.gloss: Asymptotic lower bounds Omega, tight bounds Theta and strictly smaller order o, used alongside O to compare running times.

known.name: Binary representation and bit operations
known.gloss: Writing non-negative integers (and signed ones in two's complement) as bit strings, and the bitwise operations XOR, AND and shifts, including the number of ones in a bit string.

known.name: Modular arithmetic
known.gloss: Arithmetic on integers modulo m, congruence classes, and the cyclic group Z/m under addition.

known.name: Primes, coprimality and gcd
known.gloss: Prime numbers, greatest common divisors, pairwise coprime integers, and the fact that primes of a given size are plentiful and can be found by search.

known.name: Chinese remainder theorem
known.gloss: For pairwise coprime moduli, the map from Z/(m1...mk) to the product of Z/mi given by reduction is a bijection (ring isomorphism).

known.name: Roots of unity
known.gloss: The complex solutions of z^n = 1, namely e^{2πik/n}, with Euler's formula e^{iθ} = cos θ + i sin θ and the fact that their powers sum to zero in the nontrivial case.

known.name: Vectors, matrices and invertibility
known.gloss: Vectors, linear maps and matrices over R, C or F2, matrix products and inverses, triangular and permutation matrices, and linear combinations.

known.name: Finite field F2 arithmetic
known.gloss: The field with elements 0 and 1 in which addition is XOR and multiplication is AND, over which vector spaces of bit vectors are studied.

known.name: Permutations and Cartesian products
known.gloss: Bijections of finite sets, product index sets [a1]x...x[at], and listing multi-indexed arrays in lexicographic (row-major) order.

known.name: Floor, ceiling and summation notation
known.gloss: Rounding down and up, finite and geometric sums, and indicator notation.

known.name: Recurrences and induction
known.gloss: Defining a cost by a recurrence, bounding it by induction or unrolling, and the divide-and-conquer pattern T(n) = aT(n/b) + f(n).

known.name: Norms, absolute values and error bounds
known.gloss: The modulus of a complex number, the maximum norm of a vector, the triangle inequality, and how to bound accumulated rounding errors and then round to the nearest integer.

known.name: Fast Fourier transform and divide and conquer
known.gloss: The standard O(n log n) evaluation of a length-2^k DFT by splitting into halves, and its use to multiply polynomials via pointwise products.

known.name: Sorting and data movement on tapes
known.gloss: Ordinary sorting and merging of lists, and the idea that a tape machine reads and writes sequentially, so rearranging data costs scans rather than random access.

known.name: Finite alphabet encodings and constant-factor simulation
known.gloss: Storing data in a fixed finite alphabet, packing a constant number of symbols per cell, and simulating one machine by another with a constant-factor time change.

known.name: Ring and group notions for polynomials
known.gloss: Sets with addition and multiplication satisfying the usual laws, polynomial reduction modulo a fixed polynomial, and maps preserving both operations.
